text:
jamie: FYI FrescoPay on prod is getting a lot of 429s right now, ~2.5k/min spikes for a few 10s at top-of-minute. customer reports user-facing failures. stack trace attached: `429 rate cap exceeded (rpm)`

matt: can you paste the gateway logs (request_id + region) and a short sample of client side timestamps? suspect minute-boundary aggregation.

jamie: pasted sample: `2026-03-18T12:00:00.001Z req=abc123 region=eu-west status=429 rpm=1200 tpm=15000`
`2026-03-18T12:00:00.002Z req=abc124 region=us-east status=200`
`2026-03-18T12:00:00.050Z req=abc125 region=eu-west status=429 rpm=1189 tpm=14980`

ryan: quick hypothesis — FrescoPay has a multi-region client pool and their LB is splitting connections: some regions aggregate into EU quota while bursts from other regions get routed there transiently. Also check if they're using HTTP/2 multiplexing — our per-connection concurrency + per-tenant RPM interacts poorly with long-lived streams.

lina: asked customer: are you fanouting requests from a cron or many small workers? they replied: "we run 600 lambda pods that wake every minute to sync transactions"

matt: that explains the sawtooth. If many pods schedule at the same epoch second you get a minutely stampede. Two immediate mitigations: 1) stagger the cron (random jitter) 2) implement client-side smoothing: local token-bucket with refill_rate = X and jittered sleep on failure.

jamie: customer asked for a repro script we can run from prod to validate. ryan shared a small python snippet to simulate 600 small workers: `for i in range(600): spawn_thread(send_batch(i))` and `send_batch` does 5 parallel HTTP/2 streams each. use headers `X-Client: fresco-sync` and `X-Test: minute-stamp`.

ops-bot: rate-limit alert created -> RL-7720012345; auto-suggested playbook: smoothing + quota-request.

matt: also check their SDK retry settings — default retries without jitter can create synchronized hotspots. Ask them to enable exponential backoff + full jitter and cap max concurrency per process to ~8 streams.

jamie: ran a controlled replay from our synthetic runner (eu-west egress) and reproduced 429 pulses. Replay command used: `wrk -t50 -c400 -d30s --script minute_burst.lua http://api.redwood.test/generate` produced similar per-minute spike.

ryan: config note for eng: consider exposing per-region visible quotas in the Console for customers so they can see that EU quota is being consumed preferentially. Also a server-side smoothing option (burst window smoothing) could help for cron-like fanouts.

lina: customer accepted two short-term steps: 1) apply jitter to cron (we gave them code snippet) 2) temporary reserved RPM bump for 48h while they rollout smoothing. They requested step-by-step.

jamie: shared step-by-step we gave to customer: `1) add random delay between 0-60s to each job instance startup; 2) limit per-process concurrent requests to 6; 3) enable SDK exponential backoff (base=100ms, max=6s) with full jitter; 4) monitor Console per-route RPS and errors`

matt: I provisioned a temporary +30% RPM increase on their Dedicated pool (ticket INT-4519) — tracked in support ticket. If spikes persist we'll look at per-minute smoothing at the edge.

ryan: additional debugging tip: check the gateway `X-Rate-Limit-Trace` header we add on 429s. It includes `bucket_start` and `refill_ms`. If the `bucket_start` timestamps for many requests are identical to the second, you have a stampede.

jamie: customer reports after rollout of jitter + concurrency cap the visible spike amplitude dropped by ~85% and 429s reduced to occasional edge cases. They will keep the temp RPM bump until end of week.

lina: next steps: 1) follow up email to account manager with summary and suggestion for long-term: quota re-architecture or server-side smoothing; 2) draft KB article on "Mitigating top-of-minute 429 stampedes" with code samples and monitoring checks. Can someone own the KB?

ryan: I can draft the KB — will include repro scripts, console screenshots, header diagnostics, and suggested server-side mitigations.

matt: closing notes for SRE runbook: add a quick checklist: `- ask for client cron/worker count - ask for concurrency per process - request sample request timestamps - run synthetic replay from nearest egress - offer temporary RPM bump - recommend jitter + backoff`

jamie: thanks all. marking support ticket as "in progress" and scheduling 1:1 with FrescoPay PM to discuss longer-term quota patterns. :thumbsup:
